record.original_question: For steady incompressible Euler fields, especially in three dimensions where generic steady fields have regular torus or annulus fibrations but Beltrami fields can have complicated topology, what is the right notion of a typical steady field and of genericity?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider steady solutions of the incompressible Euler equations on a three-dimensional Riemannian manifold $M$ (possibly with boundary), i.e. divergence-free vector fields $u$ satisfying
$$\nabla_u u = -\nabla p, \qquad \operatorname{div} u = 0,$$
for some pressure function $p$. Equivalently, $u\times \operatorname{curl} u = \nabla B$ for the Bernoulli function $B = p + \tfrac12|u|^2$. Two structurally different families of steady fields are known:

(a) Fields with a non-constant Bernoulli function $B$: by the Arnold structure theorem, away from critical sets of $B$ the field $u$ is tangent to the level surfaces of $B$, and on a generic regular region these level sets are tori or annuli foliated by integral curves of $u$ (so-called "integrable" steady fields).

(b) Beltrami fields, where $\operatorname{curl} u = f\, u$ for a function $f$ (necessarily constant along trajectories); these include eigenfields of the curl operator and are known to exhibit knotted and chaotic stream lines, hence topology that is far from the torus/annulus picture.

Formulate a mathematically precise and natural notion of "typical" or "generic" steady incompressible Euler field on a three-dimensional Riemannian manifold that simultaneously accounts for both behaviors above. Specifically: identify a topology (or measure, or Baire category framework) on the space of steady Euler fields, and a corresponding notion of genericity, with respect to which one can rigorously state and, if possible, prove a dichotomy or coexistence result describing the structure of a typical steady solution (e.g. integrability with toroidal/annular fibration vs. Beltrami-type chaotic behavior).
artifact.category_tag: Steady Euler flows and Beltrami fields
artifact.status_search_result: The question of formulating the right notion of a "typical" steady three-dimensional Euler field remains open. Recent work (Enciso–Peralta-Salas and collaborators) shows that Beltrami fields generically exhibit knots and chaotic dynamics, while Arnold's structure theorem gives torus/annulus fibrations for steady fields with non-constant Bernoulli function. No accepted framework yet unifies these into a single notion of genericity for steady Euler fields.

status_evidence.title: Beltrami fields exhibit knots and chaos almost surely
status_evidence.snippet: Beltrami fields exhibit knots and chaos almost surely
status_evidence.claim: Recent results show generic/almost-sure complicated topology for Beltrami fields, illustrating part of the dichotomy that motivates the open question.

status_evidence.title: Steady Euler flows and Beltrami fields in high dimensions
status_evidence.snippet: Every volume-preserving Beltrami field is a steady Euler flow for some metric in three dimensions.
status_evidence.claim: Beltrami fields form a key class of steady Euler fields, distinct from the Arnold integrable picture.

status_evidence.title: Stability results and generalized Beltrami fields
status_evidence.snippet: Generalized Beltrami fields with nonconstant proportionality factor are rare; no general framework for genericity of steady Euler flows is established.
status_evidence.claim: There is no established notion of typical steady Euler field unifying integrable and Beltrami behaviors.
